       भावीन, नई बिदेल्लीी मं भाारत काी माननीया राष्टरपबित श्रीीमती द्रौौपदेी मंमूग द्वाारा प्रदेान बिकायाा गयाा। श्रीी सारदेा भाूषण महााल्डिं�, प्रभाारी अध्यक्ष एवीं प्रबंध बिनदेेशका एवीं
                                                                                  
       बिनदेेशका (बिवीत्त) और श्रीी रजोनीश ए. खले, बिनदेेशका (बिवीपणन) पंरस्कोार काो ग्रहाण कारते हुए।

       President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, on August 29, 2025, at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. The award was received by
       Shri S.B. Mohanty, CMD, and Shri Rajnish A. Khale, Director (Marketing).

      I.  उविर्चत माूल्य पादेानोुक्रमा                                            
          याह खंडी वि�त्तीीया साधानो ंकाे उविर्चोंत मेंूल्यो ंकाो विनधाािरिरत कारने मेंं विकाए गए विनणियाो ंऔर अनुमेंानो ंकाी व्याख्याा कारता है, विजीन्हेंं (a) उविर्चोंत मेंूल्य पंर मेंान्यता
          �ी जीाती है और मेंापंा जीाता है और (b) पंरिर�ोविधात लाागत पंर मेंापंा जीाता है और विजीनकाे विलाए वि�त्तीीया वि��रणो ंमेंं उविर्चोंत मेंूल्यो ंकाा खुलाासा भुी विकायाा
          जीाता है। उविर्चोंत मेंूल्य विनधाािरण मेंं प्रयाुक्त इनपंुटौ काी वि�श्वसनीयाता काे बारे मेंं संकाे त प्र�ान कारने काे विलाए, कां पंनी ने अपंने वि�त्तीीया साधानो ंकाो लाेखांकान
          मेंानका काे तहत विनधाािरिरत तीन स्तरो ंमेंं �गीकाृ त विकायाा है। प्रत्येेका स्तर काी व्याख्याा नीर्चोंे प्रस्तुत है।
                                                                                  
      I.  Fair value hierarchy                                                    
          This section explains the judgements and estimates made in determining the fair values of the financial instruments that
          are (a) recognized and measured at fair value and (b) measured at amortized cost and for which fair values are disclosed
          in the financial statements. To provide an indication about the reliability of the inputs used in determining fair value,
          the Company has classified its financial instruments into the three levels prescribed under the accounting standard. An
          explanation of each level follows underneath the table.                 
          स्तुर 1 - समेंान पंरिरसंपंवित्तीयाो ंयाा �ेन�ारिरयाो ंकाे विलाए सविक्रेया बाजीारो ंमेंं उ��धाृत मेंूल्य (असमेंायाोविजीत)।
                                                                                  
          Level 1 - Quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.
          स्तुर 2 - स्तर 1 मेंं �ाविमेंला उ��धाृत मेंूल्यो ंकाे अलाा�ा अन्य इनपंुटौ, जीो पंरिरसंपंवित्ती याा �ेयाता काे विलाए प्रत्येक्षा रूपं से (अथाित मेंूल्यो ंकाे रूपं मेंं) याा अप्रत्येक्षा
          रूपं से (अथाित मेंूल्यो ंसे प्राप्त) अ�लाोकानीया हं।                    
                                                                                  
          Level 2 - Inputs other than quoted prices included within Level 1 that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly
          (i.e. as prices) or indirectly (i.e. derived from prices).              
          स्तुर 3 - पंरिरसंपंवित्तीयाो ंयाा �ेन�ारिरयाो ंकाे विलाए ऐसे इनपंुटौ, जीो अ�लाोकानीया बाजीार डीेटौा (अअ�लाोकानीया इनपंुटौ) पंर आधाारिरत नही ंहं।
                                                                                  
          Level 3 - Inputs for the assets or liabilities that are not based on observable market data (unobservable inputs).

      In the course of its business, the Company is exposed primarily to credit risk, liquidity risk and market risk comprising
      of fluctuation in foreign currency exchange rate, price and interest rates which may adversly impact the fair value of its
      financial instruments. The company has a risk management policy which not only covers the foreign exchange risks but also
      other risks associated with the financial assets and liabilities such as finance lease obligations, trade and other payables.
      The Company’s principal financial assets include loans, trade and other receivables, and cash and cash equivalents that
      derive directly from its operations. The Company also holds FVTPL investments in co-operative societies and Mutual Fund.
      The objectives of the Company's risk management policy are inter-alia to ensure the sustainable business growth with financial
      stability. The Company’s senior management oversees the management of these risks.

      I.  Credit risk                                                             
          Credit risk is the risk of financial loss arising from counter party failure to repay according to the contractual terms and
          obligations. Credit risk encompasses both the direct risk of default and the risk of deterioration of credit worthiness as well
          as concentration risks. The company is exposed to credit risk from its operating activities (primarily for trade receivables)
          and from its financing activities (deposits with banks and other financial instruments).
          Credit risk management                                                  
          To manage the credit risk, the Company follows a policy primarily wherein the customers are required to make an advance
          payment before procurement of goods. Thus, the requirement of assessing the impairment loss on trade receivables does
          not arise, since the collectability risk is mitigated. Most of the Other sales to private parties are against Letter of credit
          opened by banks.                                                        
          Bank balances are held with only high rated banks and majority of other security deposits are placed with government
          agencies.

      II. Liquidity risk                                                          
          Liquidity risk is defined as the risk that the company will not be able to settle or meet its obligations on time or at a
          reasonable price. For the company, liquidity risk arises from obligations on account of financial liabilities such as finance
          lease, trade payables and other financial liabilities.                  
          Liquidity risk management                                               
          The objective of liquidity risk management is to maintain sufficient liquidity and to ensure that funds are available to
          meet short-term, medium-term and long-term requirements. The Company’s corporate treasury department is responsible
          for liquidity and funding as well as settlement. In addition, processes and policies related to such risks are overseen by
          senior management. Management monitors the Company’s net liquidity position through rolling forecasts on the basis of
          expected cash flows matching the maturity profiles of financial assets and financial liabilities.

      III. Market risk                                                            
          Market risk is the risk of any loss in future earnings in realization of economic value or in future cash flows that may result
          from a change in the price, interest rates, foreign currency exchange rate, liquidity and other market changes.
          Foreign currency risk                                                   
                                                                                  
          The company’s exposure to the risk of changes in foreign exchange rates relates primarily to the company’s operating
          activities due to major overseas sales (i.e. US dollars).               
          Hence, to combat the foreign currency exposure, the company follows a policy wherein the sale is made only on receipt of
          advance from the customers. Thus, the company is not exposed to foreign currency risk.
          Price risk                                                              
          The company is exposed to price risk from its investment in mutual fund and classified in the balance sheet at fair value
          through profit and loss.                                                
          To manage its price risk arising from the investment, the Company has invested in the mutual fund after considering its risk
          and return profile i.e. the debt profile of the mutual fund indicates that the debt has been given to creditworthy banks and
          other institutional parties.

      For the purpose of the Company’s capital management, capital includes issued equity capital and all other equity reserves
      attributable to the equity holders. The primary objective of the Company’s capital management is to maximise the shareholder
      value. The Company's objectives when managing the capital are to safeguard their ability to continue as a going concern, so that
      they can continue to provide returns for shareholders and benefits for other stakeholders. The Board’s policy is to maintain a
      strong capital base so as to maintain investor, creditor and market confidence and to sustain future development of the business.
      The Board of Directors and senior management monitors the return on capital, which the Company defines as result from
      operating activities divided by total shareholders’ equity.

      Description of segments and principal activities                            
      The company’s chief operating decision maker - Group of executive directors examines the company's performance. The
      management has identified the operating segment on the basis of review by chief operating decision maker. For management
      purposes, the Company is organised into business units based on its products ie mineral division and chemical division. Govt.of
      India vide notification no - 26/2015-2020 Dt.21-08-2018 has notified that IREL shall act upon as a State Trading Enterprises for all
      exports of Beach Sands Minerals. The operation/ transactions in this regard was initiated during the financial year 2019-20. Since
      the nature of activities are different , hence a new segment is being recognised during the financial year 2019-20. As such there
      are three reportable segments, as follows:                                  
      (a) Mineral division, which comprises of OSCOM, M.K. and Chavara units      
      (b) Chemical units, which comprises of REEP and RED units                   
      (c) Trading of Beach Sand Minerals                                          
      Revenue and expenses has been accounted on the basis of their relationship to the operating activities of the segment. Income
      and expenses, which relate to the Company as a whole and are not allocable to segments on a reasonable basis, have been
      included under “Unallocable Income" and “Unallocable Expenses" respectively. Assets and Liabilities, which relate to the enterprise
      as a whole and are not allocable to segments on a reasonable basis, have been included under “Unallocable Assets/ Liabilities”.
      Inter-segment transfers are accounted for at competitive market prices charged to unaffiliated customers for similar goods.

      Provident Fund (PF) :                                                       
      The Company manages provident fund through a provident fund trust for its employees which is permitted under the Provident
      Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952. The plan envisages contribution by employer and employees and guaranteed
      interest at the rate notified by the provident fund authority.              
      The Company has an obligation to fund any shortfall on the yield of the Trust's investments over the administered interest rates
      on an annual basis. The actuary has provided a valuation for providend fund liabilities on the basis of guidance issued by Actuarial
      Society of India and based on the below provided assumptions, there is no short fall As at 31st March 2025 and 31st March 2024.

      Post Retirement Medical Scheme (PRMS):                                      
      The post retirement medical scheme provides for reimbursement of health care costs (both domicilliary & hospitalisation) to
      employees post their retirement. The reimbursement is subject to an overall ceiling based on cadre of the employee at the time
      of retirement.

      1.  वतचमाानो अनोुपाात (आरओई)                                                
          कां पंनी ने लााभु अविजीित विकायाा है तथा �र्षि काे �ौरान काोई बड़ेा पंूंजीीगत व्यया/�ीघुिकााविलाका विन�े� नही ंहुआ, इसविलाए �र्षि काे �ौरान कां पंनी काी �तिमेंान
          पंरिरसंपंवित्ती मेंं �ृज्यिद्ध हुई, लाेविकान �तिमेंान �ेयाता लागभुग उसी स्तर पंर बनी रही, विजीसकाे पंरिरणामेंस्वीरूपं �तिमेंान अनुपंात मेंं �ृज्यिद्ध हुई है।
                                                                                  
      2.  इखिक्वटी अनोुपाात पार प्रवितफल (आरओई)                                   
          इज्यिक्वटौी पंर रिरटौनि (%) काी गणना औसत विन�ला मेंूल्य काे PAT काे प्रवित�त काे रूपं मेंं काी जीाती है। र्चोंूंविका कार काे बा� लााभु (पंीएटौी) काो विन�ला मेंूल्य मेंं
          जीोड़ेा जीाता है, पंरिरणामेंस्वीरूपं, औसत विन�ला मेंूल्य �र्षि �र �र्षि आधाार पंर संविर्चोंत होती जीाती है। र्चोंूंविका विन�ला मेंूल्य काी तुलाना मेंं पंीएटौी रैज्यिखका रूपं

          इसकाे अलाा�ा, �र्षि काे �ौरान पंरिरर्चोंालान से प्राप्त राजीस्वी काे कामें मेंूल्य काे काारण EBIT मेंं कामेंी आई है, विजीसकाे पंरिरणामेंस्वीरूपं विनयाोविजीत पंूंजीी पंर
          प्रवितफला मेंं कामेंी आई है।                                            
                                                                                  
      Reasons for 25% Increase/ (Decrease) in Ratio                               
                                                                                  
      1.  CURRENT RATIO (ROE)                                                     
          The Company earned profit and there is no major capital expenditure/long term investment during the year hence current
          asset of the company has increased during the year but current liability remains almost at same level resulted in increased
          current ratio.                                                          
      2.  RETURN ON EQUITY RATIO (ROE)                                            
          The return on Equity (%) is calculated as a percentage of PAT to average net worth. Since profit after tax (PAT) is added to
          Net Worth, as a result, the average Net worth gets accumulated year on year basis. As the PAT cannot increase linearly in
          comparison to Net Worth that resulted in decrease in Return on Equity.  
      3.  INVENTORY TURN OVER RATIO                                               
                                                                                  
          Market for Rare Earths has been witnessing a downturn since the start of financial year 2024-25 due to supply side surplus
          & economic downturn in major economies and price trend of minerals also showed reducing trend, hence sales decreased
          from the last year and increase in Inventory as compared to the last financial year indicates inefficient management of
          inventory that resulted in decrease in inventory turnover ratio.        
      4.  TRADE RECEIVABLE TURN OVER RATIO                                        
          Decrease in Trade Receivable turnover as compared to the last financial year indicates inefficient management of collection
          from debtors.

                    AmB©AmaB©Ec (B§{S`m) {c[_QoS                                  
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
      5.  TRADE PAYABLE TURN OVER RATIO                                           
                                                                                  
          Increase in trade payable turnover as compared to the last financial year indicates company is having sufficient funds in
          hand to settle its debts promptly.                                      
      6.  NET CAPITAL TURN OVER RATIO                                             
          The Company earned profit and there is no major capital expenditure/long term investment during the year hence current
          asset of the company has increased during the year but current liability remains almost at same level resulted in increased
          current ratio, accordingly working capital has increased and during the year revenue from operation has decreased as
          mention in point no. 3 above that resulted in decrease in net capital turnover as compared to the last financial year.
      7.  RETURN ON CAPITAL EMPLOYED (ROCE)                                       
                                                                                  
          Since profit after tax (PAT) is added to Net Worth, as a result, the average Net worth gets accumulated year on year basis.
          Further during the year EBIT has decreased due to lower value of revenue from operation that resulted in decrease in
          Return on capital employed

      Note 55:                                                                    
      1.  The company received a demand notice no. 584 dated 26th August 2020 from the Office of the mining Officer, Ganjam
          Circle, Berhampur, Government of Odisha demanding the payment of the Compensation of ` 4595.50 lakh related to
          recovery of price of minerals produced without/beyond the Environment Clearance (EC) alone under section 21(5) of Mines
          and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957 based on the Judgement of Honorable Supreme Court of India
          passed on 02.08.2017 in the matter of common cause Vrs. Union of India vide WP ( C) No. 114/2014. Apart from the fact
          that this decision is in respect of Iron Ore & Manganese mines of the state of Odisha and has no automatic application
          on the extracted Ilmenite, Rutile, Zircon, Sillimanite, Garnet & Monazite by the Company, the Ministry of Environment
          and Forests (MoEF) itself had vide circular dated 14.12.2006 provided that any change in the product mix or change in
          the quantity or number of products may be allowed without prior environment clearance provided such changes in the
          quantities of products are in the same category and within the previously granted overall total limits.
          The Company contested the Demand notice before the revisional authority, Department of Atomic Energy, Government of
          India and the revisional authority passed the order dated 27.07.2022 confirming the liability to pay ` 4595.50 lakh.
          The Company challenged the order dated 27.07.2022 of the Revisional Authority by way of writ petition before the High
          Court which upheld the order the revisional authority, however in the SLP filed by the Company before the Honorable
          Supreme Court of India, the Honorable Supreme Court has been pleased to stay the order of the Divisional Bench of High
          Court. The amount of ` 4595.50 lakh was deposited under protest.

          included as exceptional items in the FY 2022-23.                        
          On the request of IREL, the Ministery of Environment and Forests (MoEF) confirmed vide letter dated 10th October 2023 that
          the circular dated 14.12.2006 is applicable to the EC dated 14 May 1991 for the extant project of IREL, but refund request
          was rejected by Govt. of Odhisha vide letter dated 16th March 2024 as the matter is subjudice before Hon'ble Apext Court.

      Expected Credit Loss                                                        
      The Company uses a provision matrix to determine impairment loss on portfolio of its trade receivable. The provision matrix is
      based on its historically observed default rates over the expected life of the trade receivable and is adjusted for forward- looking
      estimates. At every reporting date, the historically observed default rates are updated and changes in forward-looking estimates
      are analyzed. The Company estimates the following matrix at the reporting date which is calculated on overdue amounts. The
      Company has no historical default rate and therefore there is no expected cedit loss against trade receivable.

      I.  Fair value hierarchy                                                    
          This section explains the judgements and estimates made in determining the fair values of the financial instruments that
          are (a) recognized and measured at fair value and (b) measured at amortized cost and for which fair values are disclosed
          in the financial statements. To provide an indication about the reliability of the inputs used in determining fair value,
          the Company has classified its financial instruments into the three levels prescribed under the accounting standard. An
          explanation of each level follows underneath the table.                 
          Level 1 - Quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.
                                                                                  
          Level 2 - Inputs other than quoted prices included within Level 1 that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly
          (i.e. as prices) or indirectly (i.e. derived from prices).              
          Level 3 - Inputs for the assets or liabilities that are not based on observable market data (unobservable inputs).

      II. Valuation technique used to determine fair value                        
          Significant valuation techniques used to value financial instruments include:
          The fair values for Security deposits, loan to employees are based on discounted cash flows using a discount rate determined
          considering the average of prevailing interest rate of SBI, average yield rate on 10 year bond, last 10 years average prime
          lending rate.

      III. Valuation processes                                                    
                                                                                  
          The finance department of the company performs the valuation of assets and liabilities required for financial reporting
          purposes. The team directly reports to the Director Finance for approval of the valuation method.
          The main Level 2 input for the valuation process are derived and evaluated as follows:
          •  Discount rates are determined considering the average of prevailing interest rate of SBI, average yield rate on 10 year
             bond, last 10 years average prime lending rate that reflect current market assessment of the time value of money and
             the risk specific to the asset.

      Note 43: Financial risk management                                          
      In the course of its business, the Company is exposed primarily to credit risk, liquidity risk and market risk comprising of fluctuation
      in foreign currency exchange rate, price and interest rates which may adversly impact the fair value of its financial instruments.
      The company has a risk management policy which not only covers the foreign exchange risks but also other risks associated with
      the financial assets and liabilities such as finance lease obligations, trade and other payables. The Company’s principal financial
      assets include loans, trade and other receivables, and cash and cash equivalents that derive directly from its operations. The
      Company also holds FVTPL investments in co-operative societies and Mutual Fund.
      The objectives of the Company's risk management policy are inter-alia to ensure the sustainable business growth with financial
      stability. The Company’s senior management oversees the management of these risks.

      I.  Credit risk                                                             
                                                                                  
          Credit risk is the risk of financial loss arising from counterparty failure to repay according to the contractual terms and
          obligations. Credit risk encompasses both the direct risk of default and the risk of deterioration of creditworthiness as well
          as concentration risks. The company is exposed to credit risk from its operating activities (primarily for trade receivables)
          and from its financing activities (deposits with banks and other financial instruments).
          ऋण �ोक्विखमें प्रबीं�नु                                                 
                                                                                  
          ऋण �ोल्डिंखामा का प्रब�धनु करनुे के निलाए, क� पूनुी माुख्य रूपू से एक नुीनित का पूालानु करती होै नि�समां ग्रीाहोको �को मााला की खारी� से पूहोलाे अनिग्रीमा भुगतानु
          करनुा आर्वश्यक होोता होै। इंस प्रकार, व्यापूार प्राप्य पूर क्षनित होानिनु का आकलानु करनुे की आर्वश्यकता नुहोी �होोती होै, क्याोनेनि�क इंसमां सामाूनिहोकता के
          �ोल्डिंखामा कमा होो �ाते हों। निनु�ी पूक्षो �को निकए �ानुे र्वालाे अनिधका�श अन्य निब�ी बंको �को र्चालाू ऋण पूत्र के आधार पूर निकए �ाते हों।
          बंक मां शेर्ष के र्वला उच्च श्रेेणी के बंको �के साथ रखाे �ाते हों और अनिधका�श सुरक्षा �माा माुख्य रूपू से सरकारी ए�नेंनिसयोो �के साथ रखाे �ाते हों।
                                                                                  
          Credit risk management                                                  
          To manage the credit risk, the Company follows a policy primarily wherein the customers are required to make an advance
          payment before procurement of goods. Thus, the requirement of assessing the impairment loss on trade receivables does
          not arise, since the collectability risk is mitigated. Most of the Other sales to private parties are against Letter of credit
          opened by banks.                                                        
          Bank balances are held with only high rated banks and majority of other security deposits are placed with government
          agencies.

      II. Liquidity risk                                                          
          Liquidity risk is defined as the risk that the company will not be able to settle or meet its obligations on time or at a
          reasonable price. For the company, liquidity risk arises from obligations on account of financial liabilities such as finance
          lease, trade payables and other financial liabilities.

          Liquidity risk management                                               
                                                                                  
          The objective of liquidity risk management is to maintain sufficient liquidity and to ensure that funds are available to
          meet short-term, medium-term and long-term requirements. The Company’s corporate treasury department is responsible
          for liquidity and funding as well as settlement. In addition, processes and policies related to such risks are overseen by
          senior management. Management monitors the Company’s net liquidity position through rolling forecasts on the basis of
          expected cash flows matching the maturity profiles of financial assets and financial liabilities.

      III. Market risk                                                            
          Market risk is the risk of any loss in future earnings in realization of economic value or in future cash flows that may result
          from a change in the price , interest rates, foreign currency exchange rate, liquidity and other market changes.

          Foreign currency risk                                                   
          The company’s exposure to the risk of changes in foreign exchange rates relates primarily to the company’s operating
          activities due to major overseas sales (i.e. US dollars).               
          Hence, to combat the foreign currency exposure, the company follows a policy wherein the sale is made only on receipt of
          advance from the customers. Thus, the company is not exposed to foreign currency risk.

      Note 44: Capital management                                                 
                                                                                  
      For the purpose of the Company’s capital management, capital includes issued equity capital and all other equity reserves
      attributable to the equity holders. The primary objective of the Company’s capital management is to maximise the shareholder
      value. The Company's objectives when managing the capital are to safeguard their ability to continue as a going concern, so that
      they can continue to provide returns for shareholders and benefits for other stakeholders. The Board’s policy is to maintain a
      strong capital base so as to maintain investor, creditor and market confidence and to sustain future development of the business.
      The Board of Directors and senior management monitors the return on capital, which the Company defines as result from
      operating activities divided by total shareholders’ equity.

      Note 45: Segment information                                                
      Description of segments and principal activities                            
      The company’s chief operating decision maker - Group of executive directors examines the company's performance. The
      management has identified the operating segment on the basis of review by chief operating decision maker. For management
      purposes, the Company is organised into business units based on its products i.e. mineral division and chemical division. Govt.of
      India vide notification no-26/2015-2020 Dt.21-08-2018 has notified that IREL shall act upon as a State Trading Enterprises for all
      exports of Beach Sands Minerals. The operation/ transactions in this regard was initiated during the financial year 2019-20. Since
      the nature of activities are different, hence a new segment is being recognised during the financial year 2019-20. As such there
      are three reportable segments, as follows:                                  
      (a) Mineral division, which comprises of OSCOM, M.K. and Chavara units      
      (b) Chemical units, which comprises of REEP and RED units.                  
                                                                                  
      (c) Trading of Beach Sand Minerals                                          
      Revenue and expenses has been accounted on the basis of their relationship to the operating activities of the segment. Income
      and expenses, which relate to the Company as a whole and are not allocable to segments on a reasonable basis, have been
      included under “Unallocable Income" and “Unallocable Expenses" respectively. Assets and Liabilities, which relate to the enterprise

      Note: A suo moto case was filed by Hon'ble NGT, Principal Bench vide Case No. 76/2019 alleging excessive mining by IREL from
      the year 2001 to 2019 imposing penalty of ₹ 293 Cr. The case has been disposed by Hon'ble NGT vide its order dated 24.03.2021
      directing Kerala State Pollution Control Board to assess the amount of compensation to be levied upon IREL for excessive mining.
      In the order, State PCB was directed to take further action of finalising the compensation according to law and file an action taken
      report. It was stated that 'assessment of compensation is underway which will take further time of 3 months’. Such 3 months’
      time got expired in June 2021. In Aug 2023, Joint committee consisting of representatives of AMD, Central & State Pollution
      Control Board was formed to review status of mining by IREL for the period from 2001 to 2019. IREL submitted its representation
      & clarification to Queries to Joint committee.                              
      As part of review process, a Sub-Committee consisting of representatives from DMG, AMD, KSPCB & NCESS visited IREL & its
      mining site during 6th to 8th Dec'23 to ascertain the facts. Sevaral correspondence was made during the year by IREL, however,
      Joint committee has not yet submitted its report. Hence quantum of penalty is not ascertainable.

      additional unit of benefit entitlement and measures each unit separately to build up the final obligation.

      मां स�र्वे�नुशीला निर्वश्लेेर्षण के माानु���ो �का पूरीक्षण करता होै।        
                                                                                  
      Sensitivity analysis is analysis which will give the movement in liability if the assumptions were not proved to be true on different
      count. This only signifies the change in the liability if the difference between assumed and the actual is not following the
      parameters of the sensitivity analysis.

      1.  The company received a demand notice no. 584 dated 26th August 2020 from the Office of the mining Officer, Ganjam
          Circle, Berhampur, Government of Odisha demanding the payment of the Compensation of ` 4595.50 lakh related to
          recovery of price of minerals produced without/beyond the Environment Clearance (EC) alone under section 21(5) of Mines
          and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957 based on the Judgement of Honorable Supreme Court of India
          passed on 02.08.2017 in the matter of common cause Vrs. Union of India vide WP ( C) No. 114/2014. Apart from the fact
          that this decision is in respect of Iron Ore & Manganese mines of the state of Odisha and has no automatic application
          on the extracted Ilmenite, Rutile, Zircon, Sillimanite, Garnet & Monazite by the Company, the Ministry of Environment
          and Forests (MoEF) itself had vide circular dated 14.12.2006 provided that any change in the product mix or change in
          the quantity or number of products may be allowed without prior environment clearance provided such changes in the
          quantities of products are in the same category and within the previously granted overall total limits.
          The Company contested the Demand notice before the revisional authority, Department of Atomic Energy, Government of
          India and the revisional authority passed the order dated 27.07.2022 confirming the liability to pay ` 4595.50 lakh.
          The Company challenged the order dated 27.07.2022 of the Revisional Authority by way of writ petition before the High
          Court which upheld the order the revisional authority, however in the SLP filed by the Company before the Honorable
          Supreme Court of India, the Honorable Supreme Court has been pleased to stay the order of the Divisional Bench of High
          Court. The amount of ` 4595.50 lakh was deposited under protest.

          In view of the above, the company made provision of Compensation of ` 4595.50 lakh and entire such provision has been
          included as exceptional items in the FY 2022-23.                        
          On the request of IREL, the Ministery of Environment and Forests (MoEF) confirmed vide letter dated 10th October 2023 that
          the circular dated 14.12.2006 is applicable to the EC dated 14 May 1991 for the extant project of IREL, but refund request
          was rejected by Govt. of Odhisha vide letter dated 16th March 2024 as the matter is subjudice before Hon'ble Apext Court.
